subject: Hourly -> per-request transition: missing request IDs in usage export and reconciliation ask
messages:
From: Aditi Sharma <aditi@streamex.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: accounts-payable@streamex.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Question on Oct invoice — missing request IDs in export

Hi Rafael,

We received invoice #SE-1026 for October and our AP team cannot reconcile the charges with our internal telemetry. The usage-export you provided is missing request identifiers for roughly 18% of the records in the 10/28–10/31 window, which makes it impossible for us to trace the activity back to job IDs or customers.

Background: last month we switched to per-request attribution (from hourly rollups) as part of our migration, and we expected the token mapping to include an anonymized request_id column. The CSV you sent appears to collapse many of those rows (request_id blank / anonymized) and the totals on the invoice are ~18% higher than our own counters.

We need:
- A breakdown of the 10/28–10/31 usage by request_id or a reconciled mapping to our job ids.
- An explanation for why request_id is missing / anonymized in the export.
- Confirmation whether Redwood will provisionally credit the disputed amount while this is investigated — AP is preparing to withhold payment for the disputed portion if we can’t reconcile.

I’m attaching the invoice and the export we received. Please escalate to billing/engineering and let us know ETA — we need to settle the payment by 11/10.

Thanks,
Aditi Sharma
Director, Finance Ops
StreamEx Inc.
attachments: invoice-202610.pdf (pdf), usage-export-202610.csv (csv)

From: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Aditi Sharma <aditi@streamex.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on Oct invoice — missing request IDs in export

Hi Aditi — thanks for flagging and sorry for the friction. I’ve looped in Ben (billing ops) and Kimberly (tax & billing policy) so we can work through the reconciliation and VAT implications.

Initial read: we recently flipped the attribution pipeline from hourly-rollup IDs to per-request IDs; that migration included a short-lived aggregator (request-id indexer) that applied a 2-minute TTL before persisting IDs into the long-term rollup. Early evidence from our side suggests some late-arriving events at the tail of daily windows were anonymized by the indexer TTL and therefore showed up as "blank" request_id in the exported hourly snapshots — that can cause double-counting across the window edge in the tokenizer.

What I’m doing now:
- Ben will pull the raw aggregator logs and run a reconciliation against the source event stream (we have a debug export link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/recon/request-id-logs-20261102).
- If we confirm misattribution, Redwood will propose a provisional credit for the disputed delta and issue an updated invoice.
- Kimberly will advise on EU VAT handling if the adjustment touches October tax period.

Can you confirm the StreamEx internal job_id column name you’d like matched (job_id, run_id, or trace_id)? That will help us return a reconciled mapping.

I’ll follow up with a more specific timeline by EOD tomorrow.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
phone: +1 (415) 555-0126

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditi Sharma <aditi@streamex.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on Oct invoice — missing request IDs in export

Rafael / Aditi — quick technical summary from the ops side.

Summary of root cause (short): during the attribution rollout we introduced an in-memory request-index with a TTL of 120s to reduce persistent writes. Events that arrived after the hourly window cutoff but before the index TTL expired were being reconciled into the previous hour in our streaming join; however, when the daily CSV export was generated the export pipeline queried the hourly-rollup table and treated blank request_id buckets as "anonymous" and then re-apportioned tokens using per-hour averages. Edge-case: if an event arrived once to the streaming join but was re-emitted (duplicate) or arrived after a partition rebalance, the aggregator sometimes emitted a null request_id on the persisted rollup and the export dedup logic counted the token twice across two adjacent buckets.

What I pulled and what you’ll see:
- A sample reconciler export (reconciliation-sample.csv) that maps event_timestamp, request_id_candidate, source_event_id, token_count, and the per-hour bucket id.
- A small set (~1.8% of rows in the sample) where source_event_id duplicates map to two different hour buckets and one copy has a blank request_id. Those rows explain a ~12–20% variance depending on load shape.

Proposed remediation and short-term billing action:
1) We’ll run the full reconciliation for 10/28–10/31 and produce a line-by-line mapping to your job_id (you told us job_id = run_id in your last note).
2) We will issue a provisional credit equal to the reconciled over-bill amount and send an invoice revision within 5 business days.
3) If you prefer, we can freeze the disputed portion in collections (provisional billing hold) pending reconciliation so AP doesn’t need to withhold the full invoice.

Example reconciliation query (for your team):
SELECT source_event_id, COALESCE(request_id_candidate, 'ANON') as request_id, run_id, token_count, hour_bucket
FROM reconciliation_export
WHERE hour_bucket BETWEEN '2026-10-28T00:00Z' AND '2026-10-31T23:59Z';

I’m attaching the sample export. Rafael — request BenOps-run-full-recon and route results to Aditi.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Billing Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
attachments: reconciliation-sample.csv (csv)

From: Aditi Sharma <aditi@streamex.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, accounts-payable@streamex.com
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on Oct invoice — missing request IDs in export

Ben / Rafael — thanks for the quick investigation and for the proposed remediation steps. We confirm run_id is the column to match against.

We accept the proposed workflow: please run the full reconciliation for 10/28–10/31, produce the line-by-line mapping to our run_id, and provide a provisional credit note tied to the revised invoice. We would prefer Redwood to place the disputed portion on billing hold while the reconciliation completes — AP will then pay the undisputed remainder of the invoice on schedule.

Additional ask: the disputed amount impacts our October VAT filing in the EU; can Kimberly confirm whether Redwood will provide a credit note with VAT breakdown so our tax team can make the appropriate adjustment? If needed we can sign a short attestation accepting Redwood’s reconciliation numbers.

Provisional timeline acceptable: reconciliation results + provisional credit note by EOD 11/09. Please confirm.

Best,
Aditi
Director, Finance Ops
StreamEx Inc.
